note: Clean pass, one caveat (administered language). MAPPING data_labels and exempt from Step 5b: the S1 Table deposit (journal.pone.0194559.s002, .xlsx) carries an Excel CELL COMMENT on each header cell of row 1, and the comments on AT1..BC1 give one GSE sentence per column -- AT1 'I can always manage to solve difficult problems if I try hard enough.' .. BC1 'I can usually handle whatever comes my way.' Level checked: sharedStrings has no item text (0 CJK, headers only) and there are no SPSS-style variable labels; the wording is in xl/comments1.xml, which also supplies the covariate value labels. CODE DERIVATION is core-model pattern 1: data/liu_2018_shyness_battery.py melts the explicit by-name list SCALES['liu_2018_gse'] = [f'self_efficacy{i:02d}' for i in 1..10] with var_name='item', so the IRW item code IS the .xlsx column name -- no rename, no positional step, and the comment is attached to that very column. 10/10 columns commented. CROSS-CHECK (not needed for the exemption, run anyway): the 10 comments reproduce the canonical English GSE (Schwarzer & Jerusalem 1995, userpage.fu-berlin.de/~health/engscal.htm) word for word in canonical item order, and the paper's quoted sample item 'I can usually handle whatever comes my way' is that page's item 10 verbatim. Per-item live means also track the Hong Kong subsample (n=1067) of Schwarzer's 24-nation GSE .sav, whose columns self1..self10 carry the same canonical wording as variable labels: Spearman 0.976 over the 10 item means (live 3.40/3.00/2.61/2.93/2.86/3.31/3.16/2.99/3.23/2.77 vs HK 2.76/2.35/1.78/2.09/2.03/2.82/2.40/2.35/2.53/1.94), and the inter-item correlation matrices agree at r=0.807 under the identity mapping against a random-permutation null of mean 0.001 (0 of 20,000 permutations reached 0.807). OPTIONS: the paper states the coding outright -- '10 items rated on a 4-point scale (1 = Not at all true, 2 = Hardly true, 3 = Moderately true, 4 = Exactly true)' -- matching the canonical GSE response format; direction corroborated in the deposit, where the raw 10-item sum correlates -0.395 with the 13-item shyness sum and +0.344 with the SWLS sum, i.e. resp 4 is the high-efficacy end. LANGUAGE/FALLBACK: 208 working adults in Shanghai, and the paper's GSES reliability citation is to Wang, Hu & Liu's Chinese-version validation, so the administration was Chinese; the deposit and the article contain no Chinese text at all (checked: every one of the 363 CJK characters in the .xlsx XML is the font name '宋体' in styles/comment rich-text runs -- no comment string and no cell value contains CJK; the scraped article text contains 0), and the only other supplements are a TIF figure and the IRB approval PDF. So the English deposit wording goes in the base fields, the _translated columns stay empty, and text_source=translated_substitute / translation_source=study_supplied. RIGHTS: no block. Schwarzer's GSE FAQ (userpage.fu-berlin.de/~health/faq_gse.pdf) states 'We hereby grant you permission to use and reproduce the General Self-Efficacy Scale for your study, given that appropriate recognition of the source of the scale is made'; no fee, no non-commercial clause, no no-redistribution clause anywhere in the FAQ, and the deposit itself is CC BY 4.0 (PLOS ONE). STEP 3b: matches -- 10 items, resp 1-4, and the item content is GSE, not one of the five other scales in the same file.
